kyoto_sushi_kappo_matsubara_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. Nigiri sets of tuna, sea bream, yellowtail, salmon and eel with rolls and a fish-bone soup (reviews); soy sauce and the eel are usual wheat sources at sushi counters, and no gluten information is published.
kyoto_sushi_kappo_matsubara_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi counter whose sets are fish, roe and eel with a fish-bone soup (reviews). Cucumber rolls come in one set, but no vegan information is published.
kyoto_sushi_kappo_matsubara_shinmachi.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–22:30 (Tabelog). Reservations taken (Tabelog). Several reviewers say the owner now caters mainly to overseas visitors: Japanese customers are turned away at dinner and may only come at lunch (January 2025, June 2025, August 2026 reviews), and some Japanese diners have been turned away at times (August 2026). In April and July 2024 diners were told on arrival that lunch was no longer served and were offered the regular menu or the ¥3,000 set. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). About 10 counter seats on the ground floor, the upper floor once used for banquets (November 2023); the banquet plans have ended (January 2025). Smoking allowed per Tabelog (check with the shop). No parking (Tabelog). About 8 minutes from subway Shijo station (November 2023 review), on Matsubara-dori west of Shinmachi.
kyoto_sushi_kappo_matsubara_shinmachi.notes: [Sushi · Matsubara-Shinmachi, a one-man counter for visitors] An old neighbourhood sushi counter on Matsubara-dori where a veteran owner-chef works alone, serving generous nigiri sets of tuna, eel, yellowtail and sea bream with a fish-bone soup. Once a ¥1,100 lunch bargain; since 2024 the sets run about ¥2,000–3,300 and, by several reviewers’ accounts, dinner is for overseas visitors only, with Japanese diners welcome at lunch. English menu on the wall; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers describe the owner running the counter alone because no part-time help could be found (November 2023), and a 72-year-old chef working alone with one part-timer in the evenings, after years with two people (January 2025). The January 2025 reviewer reports the chef’s own explanation: Japanese and other Asian customers know the traditional ways of ordering sushi, which means detailed orders and a wide range of preparation that has become physically hard at that age, while most overseas visitors are happy with tuna and salmon; so the shop now focuses on overseas customers, raised its lunch prices, turns Japanese customers away at night and has dropped its banquet plans. An April 2024 diner was told that more foreign visitors were coming and they were easier to cater to. Reviewers also call the owner stern-looking but kind (November 2023), lively and welcoming (August 2023), very friendly and kind (August 2026), and fast at serving (March 2024). Criticism: an April 2024 diner found the rice under-seasoned and was bothered by flies; a July 2024 diner found the counter and cloth not clean, no explanation of the toppings, and loud talk with regulars, but the sushi delicious. A July 2024 diner was brought by a friend who had seen the shop on TV for its cheap, good sushi; a January 2025 visitor found it on Instagram.
chef_bio.specialty: Nigiri sets with eel and chutoro; fish-bone soup.

anecdotes.text: A November 2023 diner, the first customer of the day, paid with a ¥5,000 note; the owner for a moment asked whether it had been ¥10,000, and the honest answer reminded the reviewer of the fable of the golden and silver axes.
A June 2023 diner counted the nigiri in a ¥1,100 set and got 12 pieces instead of 10, unsure whether it was a mistake or generosity.
An April 2024 diner noticed the menu and portions seemed to change with the chef’s mood each day, and was amused to see the laid-back owner cleaning up as new customers came in.

kyoto_roots_of_all_evil_tower_sando.gf_detail: Ask: a craft-gin bar; the cocktails use herbs, spices, roots and bark (Tabelog; March 2026), and a gin highball was made with an imo shochu base (February 2025); snacks are served (2023–2025 reviews); no gluten-free information stated.
kyoto_roots_of_all_evil_tower_sando.vegan_detail: Ask: gin cocktails and non-alcoholic cocktails made with botanicals (Tabelog; 2022–2026 reviews); the snacks are not described; no vegan option stated.
kyoto_roots_of_all_evil_tower_sando.hours_raw: Tabelog: daily 11:00–23:00; closing days may vary. No reservations (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR payments accepted; non-smoking (Tabelog). A standing bar with a counter in the basement food hall of Kyoto Tower Sando (Tabelog; October 2024); you can also order and drink at the food-hall seats (March 2026). Quiet at lunchtime, busier in the evening (December 2023; October 2024); the counter is often full (March 2026). Linked to Kyoto Station by an underground passage (September 2023).
kyoto_roots_of_all_evil_tower_sando.notes: [Gin bar · Kyoto Tower Sando, a craft-gin stand] Craft gins and botanical cocktails, such as THE ROOTS with burdock and dandelion root, at a standing counter in the food hall under Kyoto Tower; staff help you choose by taste, and there are non-alcoholic cocktails. Open 11:00–23:00, no bookings.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog describes an interior inspired by roots drawing water from the earth. Reviewers praise staff who help guests choose a gin by taste and talk about the gins (October 2022 to September 2026), "a young male staff member" who explained gins and their regions (November 2025), and friendly female staff (May 2025). A Shiga regular has logged eleven visits from October 2022 to September 2026. The bar is popular with foreign tourists (January 2025; March 2026), and suits a drink before a train (January, November 2025).
chef_bio.specialty: Craft gin and botanical gin cocktails.

anecdotes.text: September 2025: "In a glass resembling an aquarium, herbs gently float, creating a drink that feels like an aquatic experience."
November 2025: "I requested a refreshing, dry gin that would hit the throat, and the staff recommended a gin and tonic made with "Sakurao" from Hiroshima."
March 2026: "It's quite popular among foreign tourists, and the counter is usually full."

kyoto_yakiniku_roman_pop_sanjokai.gf_detail: Ask. The meat comes pre-seasoned in a marinade (momi-dare), with a homemade dipping sauce and a lemon-and-broth “washing” sauce (arai-dare) on the side; the menu also has ramen, gyoza and bibimbap. No gluten information (Tabelog; 2022–2025 reviews).
kyoto_yakiniku_roman_pop_sanjokai.vegan_detail: Ask. A yakiniku shop: the Tabelog menu’s vegetable section has salted cabbage, grilled sweet potato and corn, lettuce wraps, namul and kimchi, but nothing is described as vegan and the soups are egg, wakame or beef-tail (Tabelog menu 2022).
kyoto_yakiniku_roman_pop_sanjokai.hours_raw: Monday, Wednesday–Friday 17:30–23:00; Saturday and Sunday 12:30–15:00 and 17:30–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Tuesday (Tabelog). Lunch days “not fixed”; lunch is at the counter only and booked on the day only (Tabelog). The own site gives weekday dinner 17:30–23:00 and lunch Saturday and Sunday 12:30–15:00, closed Tuesday, and may close early when ingredients run out. One October 2024 reviewer found lunch on weekends only; an October 2025 reviewer arriving at 12:30 on a holiday was asked whether no lunch was all right. Payment: cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX), e-money and QR codes on Tabelog and cards on the own site, but an October 2025 reviewer found a cash-only sign at the entrance and cards not accepted; a December 2020 reviewer saw a 10% discount for cash. 29 seats: 8 at the counter, two tatami tables for four and two tables for six; private hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). One parking space (Tabelog). Dogs by phone booking only, one seat at the ground-floor counter, pet diaper required (Tabelog). Children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). Opened 22 June 2018 (Tabelog). 430 m from Nijojo-mae station (Tabelog).
kyoto_yakiniku_roman_pop_sanjokai.notes: [Kyoto-style yakiniku · Sanjo-kai arcade, open to 23:00] A yakiniku shop in a converted two-storey townhouse on the Sanjo-kai shopping street, with a counter of small grills downstairs and sunken-table and table seating above. The meat is cut to order and marinated, eaten with a homemade dipping sauce and a light lemon-and-broth washing sauce; tongue, outside skirt, offal, grilled yukhoe and a yakiniku ramen are reviewers’ picks. Easy for solo diners; weekend lunch from ¥1,200; an English-language own site that offers a lunchtime cooking class. Card payment varies by report (see hours).

chef_bio.background: Opened 22 June 2018 (Tabelog); a May 2019 reviewer had heard of the new yakiniku shop in the Sanjo shopping street. The own site says every member of the team puts heart into the details, from the marinades to the additive-free sauces, and that the shop runs a Japanese cooking class at lunchtime. Reviews are mixed: a December 2020 diner had cold gyoza delivered first to the wrong customer without an apology and found the ramen broth weak; a July 2023 couple found many items sold out soon after opening, a slow wait and QR-code ordering hard; an October 2025 diner found the marinades too simple or too strong and the high chairs unsteady. Others praise the thick tongue, the staff cleaning the teppan (August 2022), the professional, warm staff (July 2024) and the value of the lunch (July 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: A place where everyone can gather, unwind and share a good time over grilled meat (own site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kyoto-style yakiniku with a washing sauce; yakiniku ramen.

anecdotes.text: A July 2025 diner drawn in by a ¥1,200 lunch sign outside found the counter empty at 2 pm, then watched it fill up, and was glad of the timing.
An August 2022 diner tried the ramen plain, then piled the separately served grilled meat and spicy chives on top, and planned to ask for extra chives next time.

cultural_comfort.note: The own site is in English and invites visitors to a lunchtime Japanese cooking class; ordering was by QR code in July 2023; phone may be Japanese only (Tabelog).

kyoto_tropical_cafe_shogoin.gf_detail: Ask. Rice-based plates (taco rice, gapao rice, a Taiwanese minced-meat bowl, beef-tendon bowl, hamburg steak with multigrain rice) and scones; no gluten information (2020–2026 reviews).
kyoto_tropical_cafe_shogoin.vegan_detail: Ask. The bowls and sets reviewers name are built on meat, with egg in the soup and on the Taiwanese bowl; a salad bowl with scones is on the 2026 menu, but nothing is described as vegan.
kyoto_tropical_cafe_shogoin.hours_raw: Monday–Friday 11:00–18:30; closed Saturday and Sunday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). No cards; QR payments accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking; no parking; free Wi-Fi (Tabelog). Opened 2 March 2020, a date Tabelog says it got from the manager. A March 2022 reviewer found set meals at lunch and dinner. Across from Kyoto University Hospital, about 610 m from Jingu-Marutamachi station (Tabelog; reviews).
kyoto_tropical_cafe_shogoin.notes: [Tropical café lunch · Shogoin, weekdays] A bright, wood-panelled café across from Kyoto University Hospital, open since 2020, with an Okinawan, tropical theme: taco rice, gapao rice, loco moco, a Taiwanese minced-meat bowl and homemade hamburg steak with multigrain rice, around ¥1,000–¥1,300, plus freshly baked scones and blended mango drinks. Friendly staff; portions on the light side, and service can be slow. Weekdays only; no cards.

chef_bio.background: Opened 2 March 2020 (Tabelog, from the manager). An October 2020 reviewer says it was always fully booked when it first opened; a March 2021 reviewer found two friendly staff and an Okinawan theme in a warm, wooden, sunlit room. A reviewer of seven visits (May 2023 and April 2026) comes to escape reality and notes the menu and prices changed by 2026. Some find the portions small for the price (October 2022; April 2023; August 2025) and one July 2023 diner wished the service were faster. A November 2026 reviewer heard that cakes bought to take away from the bakery next door can be eaten here.
chef_bio.specialty: Taiwanese minced-meat bowl; taco rice and gapao rice.

anecdotes.text: An April 2026 regular was told to mix the Taiwanese bowl well before eating, did so with a spoon, and found it like a bowl version of Taiwanese mazesoba, a little spicy and not greasy.
A March 2021 diner finished some errands on foot over a weekday lunch and stumbled on the café.

kyoto_martin_cafe_kojinguchi.gf_detail: Ask. Pancakes, toast, a croque madame, sandwiches, lasagna and donuts; no gluten information (Leaf 2023; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_martin_cafe_kojinguchi.vegan_detail: Ask. The plates reviewers name come with eggs, bacon, sausage or cheese; the avocado toast had cream cheese and bacon in March 2026. Nothing is described as vegan.
kyoto_martin_cafe_kojinguchi.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday 9:00–15:00 (last order 14:00); after 14:00 café menu only, with donuts the only food; closed Monday, or the next business day when Monday is a public holiday (Tabelog). Leaf Kyoto gave 9:00–17:00, closed Monday, plate meals with a drink until 14:00 and cakes and French toast after (September 2023). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog; August 2026). Tabelog says no reservations, but a November 2026 reviewer booked and found it fully booked that morning. Counter seating; no parking (Tabelog). Some steps inside; a reviewer came with a child (April 2026). Opened 23 July 2023 (Tabelog; Leaf). About 410 m from Jingu-Marutamachi station, near the Kojinguchi bus stop (Tabelog; November 2025).
kyoto_martin_cafe_kojinguchi.notes: [Brunch café · Kojinguchi, cash only] A small café with a wooden door and yellow awning on the Kamo River side of Kojinguchi, opened in 2023 on the site of the popular bakery LAND. Breakfast and brunch plates with a drink until 14:00 — pancakes with bacon, egg and chili beans, avocado toast with dukkah, croque madame — then coffee and donuts. Soft lighting, country music and friendly staff; can be full, and some find the portions light.

chef_bio.background: Opened 23 July 2023 on the site of the bakery LAND (Leaf Kyoto, September 2023; February 2025 and March 2026 reviews); an August 2026 reviewer remembers the space as a former sandwich shop. A February 2025 reviewer had heard the owner of LAND moved to Canada. Reviewers describe lovely, young, attentive staff (February 2025; January 2026) and a cosy, softly lit wooden room with country music (November 2025; January 2026). A March 2026 diner found the avocado toast nothing special, and an April 2026 diner wanted a bit more on the croque madame plate; most others found the plates filling.
chef_bio.specialty: Pancake plate; avocado toast plate.

anecdotes.text: A February 2026 diner gave up on a long queue at a nearby udon shop, remembered this café, and found it surprisingly empty at 12:30 on a holiday.
A February 2025 diner walking north along the Kamo River realised it was Kyoto Marathon day and stopped in at 1:30 pm to find many seats free.

cultural_comfort.note: Small café; Leaf Kyoto has an English page; seat yourself (January 2026).

kyoto_oryori_kasai_marutamachi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. Tabelog states the restaurant cannot accommodate allergies or disliked ingredients on the day of the reservation. The kaiseki uses soy sauce, ponzu, miso and fried courses (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_oryori_kasai_marutamachi.vegan_detail: No. The restaurant states it cannot cater to vegetarian requests (Tabelog), and the dashi is made with bonito and tuna flakes (August and September 2026).
kyoto_oryori_kasai_marutamachi.hours_raw: Dinner from 18:30 Monday, Tuesday and Friday–Sunday; lunch from 12:00 on Sunday and Tuesday only; a Kyoto breakfast at 8:00 or 9:30 once a month; closed Wednesday and Thursday (own site). Tabelog gives dinner 18:30–21:30 and lunch 12:00–15:00, lunch reservations by phone only. Reservation only, at least two days ahead, through TableCheck or by phone (own site; Tabelog). Lunch kaiseki ¥11,000 (about 2½ hours), dinner kaiseki ¥14,300 (about 3 hours), Kyoto breakfast ¥3,000, tax incl. (own site). Children from middle-school age, served the same kaiseki as adults; arriving more than 30 minutes late counts as a cancellation (Tabelog). 8 counter seats; private hire possible; cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and e-money, no QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking, with a smoking room inside (Tabelog). Coin parking nearby (Tabelog). Opening: Tabelog lists 30 August 2025 (its highlights text says August 2023); 2026 reviewers speak of a first anniversary in August 2026. About 500 m from Marutamachi station, a short walk east of Horikawa-Marutamachi (Tabelog; August 2026).
kyoto_oryori_kasai_marutamachi.notes: [Kaiseki counter · Horikawa-Marutamachi, reservation only] A calm, spacious eight-seat counter on a quiet street near Horikawa-Marutamachi, opened in 2025 by a chef with more than 20 years in Kyoto cuisine, trained in Arashiyama, Gion and Kibune (own site); the chef’s wife looks after the guests. A monthly kaiseki built on morning-made dashi, charcoal grilling and seasonal fish, ending with clay-pot rice and many toppings — ¥14,300 at dinner, ¥11,000 at the twice-weekly lunch. Book at least two days ahead; no vegetarian requests.

chef_bio.background: A cook with more than 20 years in Kyoto cuisine who trained in Arashiyama, Gion and Kibune (own site). An August 2026 reviewer says the chef was formerly head chef at a restaurant in Arashiyama; another August 2026 reviewer describes a native of Tokushima with over twenty years in kaiseki and ryotei kitchens in Gion, Arashiyama and Kibune. Reviewers in August–October 2026 describe the restaurant as run by the chef and the chef’s wife, together; a September 2026 reviewer praises the comfortable distance from the chef and the wife’s warm hospitality, and an August 2026 reviewer admired the glassware chosen by the hostess. The owner personally chooses seasonal ingredients at the market (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Depth rather than flashiness: dishes that put flavour and the ingredients first (Tabelog; August and October 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Monthly kaiseki; clay-pot rice with toppings.

anecdotes.text: An August 2026 diner, curious about a round item on the counter grill, found it was a tomato served with the Tokushima beef.
An October 2026 diner on a second visit took several helpings of rice, finishing with egg over rice and soy sauce, to the sound of recorded crickets.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (お料理かさい、京都市中京区の会席・懐石料理店): 京の名所・嵐山や祇園、貴船で腕を磨いた京料理歴20年以上の料理人、お昼の会席 11,000円 (税込、約2時間半、日・火の週2回 12:00〜)、夜の会席 14,300円 (税込、約3時間、18:30〜)、京の朝食 3,000円 (税込、月1回 8:00〜・9:30〜)、水・木曜日定休、2日前までの完全予約制、TableCheck または電話。食べログ: 日本料理・海鮮・天ぷら、中京区小川通丸太町下ル中之町73-6、丸太町駅から501m、完全予約制、当日のアレルギーや苦手な食材には対応できない、ベジタリアンやハラールにも対応できない、子どもは中学生以上で大人と同じ会席、30分以上の遅れはキャンセル扱い、8席 (カウンター)、貸切可、カード・電子マネー可、QR決済不可、禁煙 (店内に喫煙室)、近くにコインパーキング、オープン日 2025年8月30日 (紹介文には2023年8月)、店主が市場で旬の食材を選ぶ、毎朝ひく出汁、月替わりの夜の会席、京野菜、Shikoku の米。口コミ (2025〜2026年、英語、一部日本語の写真説明): 蟹の特別会席、丁寧で親しみやすい店主 (2025年12月)、料理人とおかみの温かいもてなし (2026年7月更新)、開店1周年、Tokushima 出身、祇園・嵐山・貴船の会席や料亭で20年以上、8席のカウンター、鴨ロース、賀茂なす、金目鯛の揚げ物と冬瓜の椀、鱧の梅肉、鰆の炙り、無花果の豆腐のソース、Tokushima の黒毛和牛、とうもろこしの粥、鱧と無花果の天ぷら、Handa のそうめん、金の釜の香川の米、鰻、出汁巻、ちりめん山椒、黒糖プリン、嵐山の店の料理長だった (2026年8月)、9月下旬の会席14,300円、焼き茄子のジュレ、焼き鮎の椀、縞鯵とメカジキ、Miyagi の戻り鰹、鯖寿司、蒸し鮑、甘鯛のごま焼き、熊本の赤牛、栗の粥に松茸の餡、松茸と無花果の揚げ物、土鍋ご飯、鰹の漬け、にゅうめん、手作りプリン、飲み物は一杯1,000円ほどから、夫婦で営む (2026年9月)、焼き茄子の寒天寄せ 卸し生姜と花穂紫蘇、島根県産 甘鯛と長崎県産 縞鯵の造り、名残りの松茸と鱧の土瓶蒸し、熊本県産 赤牛の炭火焼、鰆の霰揚げに空芯菜の胡麻和え、京都ポークと海老芋の白味噌、出汁巻玉子の染め卸し、香川県産の新米ごはん、杉勇 特別純米、美丈夫 純米吟醸、黒糖プリン、ほうじ茶 (2026年10月)。

kyoto_chikara_mochi_shichijo.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the core is wheat udon made from Hokkaido flour (Tabelog), with soba, curry udon and tempura udon (2024–2026 reviews); the rice bowls and inari sushi are rice but no gluten information is given.
kyoto_chikara_mochi_shichijo.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the dashi is made from Rishiri kombu and katsuobushi (Tabelog), and it goes into the noodles, the curry and the donburi (2026 reviews).
kyoto_chikara_mochi_shichijo.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 10:30–16:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog). A September 2026 reviewer gave 11:00–14:00, closed Saturday and Sunday, and a November 2026 reviewer called it lunch-only, so Saturday is left unset here — check before going. No reservations; no credit cards (Tabelog); paid in cash after eating (June 2026); e-money not stated. 32 seats: 20 at tables and 12 on tatami (Tabelog). Non-smoking; no parking, coin parking nearby (Tabelog). Shared tables at busy times (September 2026). 7 min walk from JR Kyoto Stn, on the north side of Shichijo-dori (Tabelog; April and September 2026).
kyoto_chikara_mochi_shichijo.notes: [Udon · Shichijo-dori, north of Kyoto Stn, curry udon and inari in an old diner] A long-established udon and donburi diner with tatami and table seats, seven minutes from Kyoto Station: the ¥800 curry udon with two inari sushi is what most regulars order, and the dashi is the point. Run by a friendly owner, sometimes alone. Cash only; closed Sunday; daytime only.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: the shop’s own Tabelog text says it has kept its original flavours since its founding in 1924, while Tabelog’s opening-date field gives 1 October 1938. A September 2026 reviewer traces the wider Chikara Mochi name to 1903, a name that spread across Kansai on everyday udon and donburi diners; whether this shop belongs to that line is not stated. Reviewers describe a Showa-era soba-shop interior (March 2026) behind a wooden lattice and noren (September 2026), an owner who greets guests warmly with hojicha (March 2026) and gives friendly service (August 2026), and, at 12:30 one August 2026 day, one person cooking and serving alone. Most customers seemed to be locals, with hardly any tourists (September 2026). One September 2026 diner found the noodles uniform, like frozen ones, but praised the broth.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keeps its original flavours while adding new dishes (the shop’s Tabelog text).
chef_bio.specialty: Curry udon with two inari sushi.

anecdotes.text: In March 2026 a diner came in craving katsudon, learned the shop no longer fried anything, and settled happily on meat udon and a Kinugasa-don — then watched regulars order curry udon and came back in April for it.
An August 2026 regular, first in the door just after 11, asked for an off-menu chilled sansai soba with an onigiri made to order.
A diner who had never managed to catch it open finally came on a quiet weekday in November 2026 for the curry udon set.

kyoto_utr_shijo_omiya.gf_detail: Ask. Sashimi and grilled fish sit alongside tempura, fried fish, spring rolls and dashi omelette (2025–2026 reviews); no gluten information.
kyoto_utr_shijo_omiya.vegan_detail: Ask. The menu centres on fish, but there are vegetable dishes such as maitake tempura (July 2025), turnips sautéed in butter and soy sauce (January 2026) and a strawberry-kumquat salad with mascarpone (March 2026); no vegan dish is described.
kyoto_utr_shijo_omiya.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday and public holidays 18:00–24:00 (last order 23:30); closed Monday and the day after a public holiday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, including through Tabelog (Tabelog; October 2025); it filled up one December 2025 night. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and e-money (transport IC, QUICPay) accepted; no QR (Tabelog). 12 seats: 8 at the counter and a table for 4 (Tabelog). Non-smoking; no parking, coin parking nearby (Tabelog). Opened 5 May 2025 (Tabelog). On the second floor of 坊城ビル, whose ground floor is SOUTH BOUND KYOTO (kyoto_south_bound, address_ja "壬生坊城町55 坊城ビル 1F"); the entrance is a little hard to find (January 2026). 3 min walk from Shijo-Omiya (Tabelog).
kyoto_utr_shijo_omiya.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo-Omiya, fish and inventive small plates upstairs] A twelve-seat second-floor izakaya opened in May 2025 by an owner who used to run a fish shop: sashimi platters, eel-and-cucumber spring rolls, eel on dashi omelette, seasonal tempura, with sake and craft beer by the half glass. Solo-friendly; open to midnight. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: opened on 5 May 2025. An October 2025 diner learned that the owner used to run a fish shop, and a July 2025 diner that the owner had worked at another restaurant before. Reviewers describe a stylish, calm room with soft lighting and a window onto the back alley (October 2025; March 2026), roomy counter seats (October 2025), pop music playing (January 2026), and a friendly owner who chats with solo guests (October 2025; March 2026). A January 2026 diner noted that the place is run by one person, so the sashimi came only after a large beer was finished, and was disappointed that there was no starter and that the beer was not ice-cold.
chef_bio.specialty: Fish dishes; eel-and-cucumber spring rolls.

anecdotes.text: An October 2025 couple worked through eight dishes; the owner also sliced some yellowtail being tried for a new dish that was not yet on the menu.
In June 2026 a diner who meant to stop in briefly for a second round stayed long over the spring rolls and canelés.
A March 2026 visitor wanted the salted-milk yoghurt sake, found it sold out, and took the yoghurt one instead.

kyoto_bar_island_kyoto_station.gf_detail: Ask. A cocktail and whisky bar: over 200 drinks, including fresh-fruit cocktails, Scotch, bourbon, brandy and wine (Tabelog), with snacks such as a ham-and-salami platter (September 2024) and chocolate (December 2021); no gluten information.
kyoto_bar_island_kyoto_station.vegan_detail: Ask. The fresh-fruit cocktails and spirits are the point (Tabelog; 2021–2026 reviews); the food mentioned is cured meat and chocolate (2021; 2024); no vegan information.
kyoto_bar_island_kyoto_station.hours_raw: Monday–Thursday and Sunday 19:00–2:00; Friday, Saturday and the day before a public holiday 19:00–4:00; open year-round except 31 December and 1 January (Tabelog). Cover charge ¥500 per person (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) accepted (Tabelog). 24 seats: 8 at the counter, two tables for 4 and a semi-private room for 8; private hire for 20–50 (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog; September 2024). On the second floor of エムワンビル in front of Kyoto Tower, 1–2 min from the Karasuma Central Exit of Kyoto Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_bar_island_kyoto_station.notes: [Bar · in front of Kyoto Tower, fruit cocktails until late] A calm, dimly lit cocktail bar on a second floor by Kyoto Station, open since 2008 and until 2:00 (4:00 on Fridays and Saturdays) — rare near the station. Over 200 drinks, fresh-fruit cocktails and its own gin; ¥500 cover; smoking allowed. Open year-round.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: opened on 21 April 2008 a short walk from Kyoto Station, as a simple, classic bar for dates and travellers (Tabelog). Reviewers describe a calm room with soft lighting (2024; July 2026), a friendly master (February 2023; September 2024; October 2026) and bartenders who keep a pleasant distance while chatting (May 2024). In October 2026 it was run by the master and a female staff member, both easy to talk to. A January 2020 diner disliked how actively the bartender asked guests for the next order, and an April 2017 diner was disappointed by plastic glasses. A July 2026 visitor found it busy late on a weekday and valued a bar near the station that stays open late.
chef_bio.specialty: Fresh-fruit cocktails; house gin.

anecdotes.text: In October 2026 a first-time visitor praised the sansho in the house spice gin and tonic and was told, with a smile, that there was no sansho in it; a martini order brought the bar’s stock joke, “just a little martini”.
A December 2021 couple made this the third bar of the night: neat Glenmorangie, then a Glen Grant on the bartender’s advice, with two fruit cocktails, for about ¥8,000.
After a first and a second party in May 2024, a group searched around Kyoto Station for somewhere still open late, ended the night here, and liked the kiwi cocktail.

kyoto_restaurant_passion_kojinguchi.gf_detail: Ask. Lunch comes with soup and either bread — a baguette and a rice-flour bread (2021–2024 reviews) — or rice (November 2024); mains are fish, pork, beef and mussels (2021–2025 reviews), and fried oysters appear in season (March 2024). No gluten information.
kyoto_restaurant_passion_kojinguchi.vegan_detail: Ask. The courses are built around fish and meat (2021–2026 reviews); vegetable soups such as beet, pumpkin and squash are served (2022–2024), but no vegan dish is described.
kyoto_restaurant_passion_kojinguchi.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:00) and dinner 17:30–22:00 (last order 21:00); closed Monday, open on a Monday public holiday and closed the next day (Tabelog; Retty). Reservations accepted (Tabelog) and advised: full with bookings on a Saturday in October 2022 and a rainy day in November 2026; private hire possible (Tabelog; November 2025). No credit cards (Tabelog) and no e-money (April 2020 review). 22 seats: 2 at the counter and 20 at tables (Tabelog: "10 seats at the table x 2"). Non-smoking; children welcome; no parking, coin parking nearby (Tabelog). Opened 17 September 2010 (Tabelog). 1 min walk east of the Kojinguchi bus stop on Kawaramachi-dori, 5 min from Jingu-Marutamachi Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_restaurant_passion_kojinguchi.notes: [French · Kojinguchi, couple-run bistro lunches near the Kamo River] A homely 22-seat French bistro a minute east of Kawaramachi at Kojinguchi, run by the chef and the chef’s wife since 2010: lunches of soup, a main of three fish or three hors d’oeuvres, and warm rice-flour bread for about ¥1,450, with meat courses at night. Book ahead; cash only. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: opened on 17 September 2010 (Tabelog). A March 2024 diner called it a very homely place run by a couple; in November 2024 the chef and the chef’s wife were the only two in the kitchen, timing each dish well; in November 2026 the chef seemed calm and the chef’s wife friendly. An April 2020 regular of about five years liked the two owners and noted that the shop does little marketing. Reviewers praise the prices and the bread (2014–2026); in September 2024 a returning diner found prices had risen quite a bit, and an August 2022 diner found the cauliflower a little soggy. Retty describes it as a casual French restaurant of quality.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch sets of fish or three hors d’oeuvres.

anecdotes.text: A November 2024 diner, sent by a taxi driver known for Kyoto restaurant tips, booked by phone, was shown how to lift the mussel shells with tongs, and was told on leaving that oysters would soon be in.
In August 2022 a diner booked at the last minute from Demachiyanagi, walked along the Kamo River in the sun, and called the chorizo perhaps the best ever.
A party of ten hired the whole room for an early year-end party in November 2025, at ¥5,000 a head before drinks.

kyoto_en_shijo_omiya.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free claim. Pasta and pizza are on the menu (2015, 2019, 2025 reviews), and a gratin was a September 2024 dish; small plates like prosciutto and salads are also served.
kyoto_en_shijo_omiya.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: no vegan claim. Dishes reviewers had are mostly cheese, meat or seafood — prosciutto, a scallop and crab-miso gratin, a blue-cheese potato salad (2022–25); baked vegetables and a bagna cauda were on an older menu (2015).
kyoto_en_shijo_omiya.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 18:30–02:00; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Cards accepted, QR not (Tabelog). 8 seats: 4 at the counter, 4 in the hall; smoking allowed; no minors; no parking (Tabelog). No restroom inside — guests use a shared one outside (April 2021, January 2025). 5 minutes’ walk from Hankyu Omiya Station (Tabelog).
kyoto_en_shijo_omiya.notes: [Italian bar · Shijo-Omiya] A bright, glass-fronted little wine bar at the entrance of the Shijo-Omiya drinking streets: ¥600 glasses of wine, bottles from about ¥2,000, prosciutto sliced to order, pasta and inventive small plates, at a counter and a few seats. Open 18:30–02:00; closed Sunday. No restroom inside (a shared one outside).

chef_bio.background: A long-running bar: reviews go back to July 2014, when a diner who left shopping bags behind was treated very kindly by the owner. A November 2014 visitor found it run by one man alone and praised the young owner’s service. Later reviewers describe a stylish bar with a handsome owner and many regulars (January 2025), and friendly, lively staff (September 2024, April 2025); glass doors let you see inside before going in (2019).
chef_bio.specialty: Wine by the glass and small Italian plates; seasonal prosciutto.

anecdotes.text: In July 2014 the entrance carried a sign welcoming guests to drop in for just one drink.
A January 2025 reviewer advised coming with someone who knows the place, since there are many regulars, and using the restroom before arriving.

kyoto_hamachan_rido.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free claim. There is no menu to choose from: each drink comes with a small plate of three dishes picked by the owner — vinegared octopus, spleen with ponzu and fried saury (January 2022), a green-onion omelette (September 2025) — and ponzu and frying are both involved.
kyoto_hamachan_rido.vegan_detail: Not vegan: there is no menu to choose from, and the omakase small plates reviewers describe are octopus, spleen, saury and egg dishes (2022, 2025). No vegan claim.
kyoto_hamachan_rido.hours_raw: Hours not given on Tabelog or in reviews. Reservations taken; private hire possible (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Smoking allowed; no parking (Tabelog). A tiny counter that fills with about five people (September 2025). In the Rido dining alley (リド飲食街) on the south side of Shichijo-dori west of Karasuma, about 10 minutes’ walk from Kyoto Station; the alley’s toilets are shared and outside (December 2025). 422 m from Kyoto Station (Tabelog).
kyoto_hamachan_rido.notes: [Izakaya · Rido dining alley, Karasuma-Shichijo] A tiny counter bar in the post-war Rido dining alley, ten minutes from Kyoto Station: no menu — order a drink and the owner sets down a plate of three small dishes (sake with three dishes was ¥1,200 in November 2026), then chat over shochu from the owner’s home town in Kumamoto. Fits about five. Cash only; hours not published.

chef_bio.background: A counter shop run by the owner alone (November 2022). A December 2025 reviewer’s photo caption says the owner is from Hitoyoshi in Kumamoto and has the local shochu sent specially. Reviewers describe a laid-back, friendly owner (September 2025), a warm, laid-back owner of few words who chimes in now and then while watching TV (August 2026), a very kind voice (January 2022), and a Showa-retro feel (November 2022). A December 2025 visitor heard stories of old Kyoto and the lively past of the Rido alley; reviewers write that the alley dates from shortly after the war (September 2025).
chef_bio.specialty: A drink with an omakase plate of three small dishes; shochu from Kumamoto.

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 visitor asked for a highball, got a sweet-potato shochu highball by mistake, laughed it off, and then had a VO brandy highball instead.
In January 2022 the owner set down three dishes from the five on the counter without a word being said, and the reviewer and the owner ended up watching a TV eating contest together.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 浜ちゃん、居酒屋、京都市下京区七条通烏丸西入東境町180、京都駅から422m、営業時間の記載なし、予約可、貸切可、カード・電子マネー・QR 不可、喫煙可、駐車場なし。口コミ (2015年9月〜2026年11月、英語、写真説明は日本語): リド飲食街の小さなカウンターの店、店主ひとりで営む (2022年11月)、メニューはなく飲み物を頼むと三品盛りのつまみ、常温の日本酒と三品で1,200円 (2026年11月)、写真説明「熊本・人吉出身で地元の焼酎をわざわざ取り寄せられてます。」(2025年12月)、ビールはクラシックラガーの大瓶のみ。

cultural_comfort.note: No English evidence found; there is no menu, and the draw is conversation with the owner. Tabelog lists no hours.

kyoto_sumire_coffee_tatsumicho.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free claim. The food is baked goods — cookies, buttermilk scones and a Brazilian-style bread — and sandwiches (Leaf KYOTO; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_sumire_coffee_tatsumicho.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: no vegan claim. Black coffee is the core of the menu; the cookies are buttery (August 2025), the hot chocolate comes with vanilla ice cream (November 2025), and café au lait uses milk. Sandwiches and scones use vegetables from a nearby greengrocer (Leaf KYOTO); other ingredients not stated.
kyoto_sumire_coffee_tatsumicho.hours_raw: Weekdays 7:00–13:00; Saturday, Sunday and public holidays 9:00–16:00; closed Wednesday (Tabelog; Leaf KYOTO). Mainly take-out, with a small eat-in space where you sit side by side; order outside first, then sit (September 2025, March 2026). Non-smoking; no private rooms; no parking; no e-money (Tabelog). Photography is not allowed in some parts of the shop (Leaf KYOTO). Opened 12 July 2025 (Tabelog; Leaf KYOTO). About 9 minutes’ walk from the central gate of Kyoto Station, 7 minutes from the 烏丸七条 bus stop (Leaf KYOTO).
kyoto_sumire_coffee_tatsumicho.notes: [Café · Shinmachi-Shichijo, near Kyoto Station] A coffee stand in a renovated house over 100 years old, run by an archaeological excavation company: while your coffee is made you can look at tiles and other finds dug up during the renovation. Ice-brewed coffee, café au lait, scones and haniwa-shaped cookies (¥150). Mostly take-out, a few seats. Weekdays 7:00–13:00, weekends 9:00–16:00; closed Wednesday.

chef_bio.background: Leaf KYOTO: the café is run by a company that excavates and surveys archaeological sites (「遺跡の発掘・調査を行う会社が運営しており」); the interior is over 100 years old, and the company took it apart and renovated it itself, then put the finds from that work on display; the name comes from すみれ商店, a shop the owner’s grandmother once ran in Nara Prefecture. Reviewers: the concept is “less than a museum, more than everyday life” (August 2025); an exhibition of the company’s research — excavation plans, photos and stories from the president, who is also a field investigator (September 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: “Less than a museum, more than everyday life” (the café’s concept, as quoted in an August 2025 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Ice-brewed and hand-drip coffee; haniwa- and dogu-shaped cookies.

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 visitor gave up once after arriving at 16:00, closing time, and came back another Sunday at 14:30.
A November 2025 visitor had long wanted to come but kept missing the 13:00 weekday close.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Leaf KYOTO: すみれ珈琲、京都市下京区新町通七条上ル辰巳町747-8、遺跡の発掘・調査を行う会社が運営、築100年以上の建物を自社で解体・改修、改修で出てきた出土品を展示、店主の祖母が奈良県で営んでいた「すみれ商店」から屋号、氷出しコーヒー600円、クッキー150円 (プレーン・ココア)、近くの八百屋の野菜を使ったサンドイッチとスコーン、平日7:00〜13:00、土日・祝日9:00〜16:00、水曜休み、一部撮影禁止、2025年7月12日オープン、Instagram sumire.coffee。食べログ: すみれ珈琲、コーヒースタンド、全席禁煙。口コミ (2025年8月〜2026年6月、英語): IOLITE COFFEE ROASTERS のオリジナルブレンド、アイスカフェオレ650円、ホットチョコレート、バターミルクスコーン、テイクアウト中心で小さなイートイン。

cultural_comfort.note: No English evidence found. Order at the counter outside before sitting down.

kyoto_akemi_rido.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free claim. Homestyle dishes from a whiteboard — mini hamburg steak with ponzu, dashi-rolled omelette, grilled atsuage, lotus-root kinpira, sake-lees soup — and a macaroni-salad appetizer (2022–26 reviews); seasonings not stated.
kyoto_akemi_rido.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: no vegan claim. Most dishes reviewers had contain meat, egg or dashi — hamburg steak, dashi-rolled omelette, lotus root and pork kinpira (2023–26); grilled konjac and grilled aburaage were on the board in November 2022, ingredients not stated.
kyoto_akemi_rido.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 18:30–02:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog; the same in a September 2026 review). A December 2023 reviewer gives about 18:30 to midnight, closed Sundays and public holidays. Reservations taken (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards or e-money (Tabelog; December 2023). 8 seats at the counter; karaoke; smoking allowed; no parking (Tabelog); a 24-hour coin car park nearby at 東境町184 (September 2026). Often full of regulars; newcomers are welcomed when a seat is free (June 2026). The dashi-rolled omelette is not made when the shop is busy (September 2026). In the Rido dining alley (リド飲食街) on the south side of Shichijo-dori about 100 m west of Karasuma-Shichijo, a few minutes from Kyoto Station (2022–26 reviews); 413 m from Kyoto Station (Tabelog).
kyoto_akemi_rido.notes: [Izakaya · Rido dining alley, Karasuma-Shichijo] An eight-seat counter at the edge of the Rido dining alley near Kyoto Station, open for about twenty years: the owner cooks homestyle dishes from a whiteboard — mini hamburg steak with ponzu (¥500), dashi-rolled omelette, sake-lees soup — and there is karaoke. Newcomers welcome when there is a seat. Cash only; 18:30–02:00; closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers date the shop to about 2003 — “serving the community for 22 years” (September 2025), over 20 years with 8 seats (September 2026). Run by an energetic owner (December 2024) who cooks the homemade dishes (February 2023), with a husky voice reviewers remark on (September 2022, September 2026); a September 2025 visitor heard the owner tell how the shop came to open and found it a touching story. The owner saw a first-timer off outside (September 2022), keeps an eye on guests and suggests heading home when it is time (December 2024). Many reviewers mention a counter full of friendly regulars (2022–26). The Rido alley, reviewers write, dates from the early 1950s and is said to be named after the Lido cabaret in Paris (September 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Homestyle small dishes — mini hamburg steak, dashi-rolled omelette, sake-lees soup; karaoke.

anecdotes.text: A September 2022 first-timer sang about five Southern All Stars songs at the owner’s request as the regulars arrived and filled the counter.
In September 2026 a regular warned a newcomer that the owner skips the dashi-rolled omelette when busy; after the regular left, the newcomer asked anyway and was told “just wait a moment”.
On a full Thursday in November 2026 a regular who arrived to no seat gave up a place to a visitor and left; the owner, a little flustered, charged the visitor ¥1,000 for a drink and appetizer.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: あけ美、京都市下京区烏丸七条西入、京都駅から413m、月〜土18:30〜翌2:00、日曜休み、予約可、カード・電子マネー不可、8席、カラオケ、喫煙可、駐車場なし。口コミ (2022年9月〜2026年11月、英語、写真説明の一部は日本語): リド飲食街の家庭料理の店、ホワイトボードの品書き、お通しは手作りのマカロニサラダ、写真説明「小さなハンバーグ(※手作りですと書いてある) 500円」、だし巻き700円、粕汁、カラオケ、常連が多い、2003年ごろからの店。

kyoto_hotel_kuu_breakfast_higashihonganj.gf_detail: Ask. A buffet of sushi, Kyoto obanzai and Western dishes that includes tempura, grilled nama-fu (wheat gluten) dengaku, KUU black curry and several house natural-yeast breads (April 2024 and September 2025 reviews); no gluten or allergy information on the official site.
kyoto_hotel_kuu_breakfast_higashihonganj.vegan_detail: Ask. The October 2026 fair menu on the official site marked one dish ヴィーガン (vegan): a turnip steak. Reviews also mention an organic vegetable salad, pickles and a soy-milk medicinal porridge (April and September 2024), but no other dish is labelled and ingredients are not listed.
kyoto_hotel_kuu_breakfast_higashihonganj.hours_raw: Breakfast 7:00–10:00, WEST 1F, 40 seats (official site). Breakfast ¥2,800 tax included; a bath-and-breakfast set ¥3,280 tax included from 20 June 2026, earlier ¥2,980 (official site). Open to non-guests: a September 2024 reviewer wrote that both guests and non-guests can book, same-day walk-ins included; a September 2025 reviewer wrote that non-guests can have breakfast alone or with the bath and saw quite a few people who had come in from outside; the official site's breakfast booking link goes to no-room breakfast plans. Day-use bath: large bath ¥1,200, small bath ¥1,000 tax included from 20 June 2026, ¥100 off with your own towel; entry 6:00–9:30 and 15:00–21:30, tickets from the machine at the front desk (official site). The large and small baths swap between men and women daily (September 2024 review). Cards and QR payments accepted (Tabelog). No hotel parking; nearby coin parking (official FAQ). Children's chairs in limited number, ask ahead (official FAQ). Across from Higashi Honganji, about 7 min walk from Kyoto Station (September 2024 and September 2026 reviews).
kyoto_hotel_kuu_breakfast_higashihonganj.notes: [Breakfast buffet · Higashi Honganji] The ground-floor breakfast room of a small design hotel facing Higashi Honganji, open to non-guests: a ¥2,800 buffet of Kyoto obanzai, sushi, house breads and desserts such as an old-fashioned firm pudding, mostly made in-house, with omelettes to order and a monthly fair menu. Pair it with the hotel's day-use bath. 7:00–10:00 daily.

chef_bio.background: The official site introduces the breakfast chef without a name: born in Kyoto City, 26 years of cooking, from French restaurants, with further training in Italian cooking and at a bakery, making most of the buffet in-house and known for original desserts. The hotel is run by 株式会社インセンティア, founded September 1956, whose businesses are hotel operation, restaurants and travel planning; its company page names no other hotel (official site). Reviewers note many foreign guests (April 2024, September 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: The official site: a restaurant looking out on Higashi Honganji, pairing organic Kyoto vegetables with Japanese organic wines; breakfast of 「京のおばんざい」, gentle on the body, to start the day.
chef_bio.specialty: Obanzai breakfast buffet; old-fashioned pudding; KUU black curry.

anecdotes.text: A September 2024 visitor arrived early for the 7:00 opening, prayed at Higashi Honganji first, then took the buffet-and-bath plan, and suggested it as a stop after arriving on a night bus.

An April 2024 diner found the room small and the buffet on the light side, with nigiri sushi among the Japanese dishes because of the many foreign guests, but liked the made-to-order omelette and the pudding served on request.
A September 2025 guest lingered nearly two hours over the bite-sized dishes while looking out at Higashi Honganji.
An April 2025 visitor came for the buffet and bath to ease a tired body after a night bus.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: HOTEL KUU KYOTO、下京区不明門通正面下る卓屋町58番地。レストランの朝食「京のおばんざいを味わう朝食」7:00〜10:00、WEST 1F、40席、2,800円 (税込)。お風呂朝食セット3,280円 (税込、2026年6月20日から。それまでは2,980円)。シェフの紹介: 京都市出身、料理歴26年、フレンチレストラン出身、イタリアンやパン屋でも修行、ビュッフェのほとんどの料理を自家製手作りで提供、オリジナルデザートも得意。10月の神無月フェア: 若鶏のステーキ サルサロメスコ、もち豚の角煮と煮卵、サーモンのちゃんちゃん焼き、ヴィーガンの蕪のステーキ、もち豚の自家製プレスハム、烏賊と里芋の煮物、いろいろキノコのニラ漬け、焼き梨とモッツアレラチーズ。月の自家製オーダーデザートは南瓜のブリュレ。日帰り入浴: 大浴場1,200円、小浴場1,000円 (税込、2026年6月20日から)、受付6:00〜9:30と15:00〜21:30。会社概要: 株式会社インセンティア、創業1956年9月、ホテル運営・飲食店の経営、旅行・ツアーの企画。食べログ: カード可、QR可。口コミ (2024〜2026年、英語): 宿泊者以外も予約でき当日も可 (2024年9月)、外から朝食だけの人も多い (2025年9月)、すし、おばんざい、生麩田楽、だし巻き、KUU の黒カレー、焼きたてのオムレツ、昔ながらのかためのプリン。

cultural_comfort.note: A hotel breakfast room used by many foreign guests (April 2024 and September 2026 reviews); buffet service. Phone service may be Japanese only (Tabelog).

existence.note: Official site with 2026 prices and an October 2026 fair menu; Tabelog listing; review dated November 2026.

kyoto_marukyu_tb26036399_kawaramachi_mar.gf_detail: Ask. Grilled fish, sashimi, simmered fish in a sweet soy sauce, tempura, fried oysters and oden with fu (wheat gluten) (2024–2026 reviews); no gluten or allergy information on Tabelog.
kyoto_marukyu_tb26036399_kawaramachi_mar.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish restaurant whose set meals centre on sashimi and grilled or simmered fish with miso soup (2024–2026 reviews); no vegan dish mentioned.
kyoto_marukyu_tb26036399_kawaramachi_mar.hours_raw: Tabelog: Tue–Sun 12:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:00) and 17:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00); closed Mondays; may close temporarily. A March 2026 review copied different hours: Tue–Sat 12:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30), Sunday 12:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00, last entry 20:30), closed Mondays. Lunch is set meals only; in the evening set meals and à la carte (February 2025 review); one drink per person at dinner (March 2026 review). Reservations taken (Tabelog). Payment: Tabelog lists no cards or e-money, QR by PayPay only; the March 2026 review lists cash, cards, QR and e-money. 15 seats with a counter (Tabelog; 16 seats in the March 2026 review); shoes off before sitting at the counter (November 2026 review). Non-smoking; no parking, coin parking nearby (Tabelog). 5 min walk from Keihan Jingu-Marutamachi Stn, 15 min from Marutamachi subway Stn (Tabelog). Opened 1 November 2020 (Tabelog).
kyoto_marukyu_tb26036399_kawaramachi_mar.notes: [Fish set meals · Kawaramachi-Marutamachi] A small counter run by a couple near Kawaramachi-Marutamachi: fresh sashimi with grilled or simmered fish at lunch for about ¥1,400–1,800 with free rice refills, and in the evening tempura, oden, fried oysters and sake. Popular with regulars; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Run by a couple, with a homely feel and warm exchanges with regulars (July 2025 review). Opened 1 November 2020 (Tabelog). An April 2026 reviewer heard the chef, a keen angler, chatting with regulars about octopus fishing and a planned trip to Akashi; a November 2026 reviewer credited the quality of the fish to the owner's dedication.
chef_bio.specialty: Grilled fish and sashimi set meals; seafood rice bowl.

anecdotes.text: A July 2025 diner ordered the ¥1,800 sashimi and grilled fish set, was served the mini version, and at the till the couple apologised and charged ¥1,350 instead.
A lunchtime regular who came every two weeks tried the evening for the first time in November 2024, with Awaji anago and white eggplant tempura and oden of yuba and fu.
At the till in April 2026 a diner mentioned growing up on Awaji Island eating sea bream, conger eel and octopus every day, after hearing the chef talk about octopus fishing.
On a Sunday just after noon in September 2026 the room was almost full; the diner watched regulars check the day's fish and order the spare ribs instead.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 大将割烹 マルキュウ、居酒屋、上京区俵屋町436-3 1F、京阪「神宮丸太町駅」から徒歩5分。火〜日 12:00〜15:00 (L.O. 14:00)、17:00〜22:00 (L.O. 21:00)、月曜休み。予約可、カード・電子マネー不可、QRは PayPay、15席 (カウンターあり)、貸切可、禁煙、駐車場なし (近くにコインパーキング)、オープン 2020年11月1日。口コミ (2024〜2026年、英語): 夫婦で営む家庭的な店 (2025年7月)、店の前に手書きの黒板のメニュー、昼は定食のみ、夜は定食と一品料理、夜はワンドリンク制 (2026年3月)、ごはんのおかわり自由。焼き魚と刺身の定食1,380〜1,800円、子持ちガレイの煮付けと刺身1,480円、カキフライ定食、海鮮丼2,500円、天ぷら、おでん、とり天のタルタル1,100円、スペアリブ1,680円。

cultural_comfort.note: A small counter of regulars with a handwritten Japanese blackboard menu (July 2025 review); no English menu noted. Phone service may be Japanese only (Tabelog).

kyoto_chinon_nijojo_kojocho.gf_detail: Ask. House bread with every lunch, a Kamo eggplant gratin, seafood risotto, terrine and sauced meat dishes (official menu; 2022 and 2023 reviews); no gluten or allergy information.
kyoto_chinon_nijojo_kojocho.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan dish is marked; the menu is built on meat, fish, oysters, foie gras and cheese (official menu). The gazpacho, a chilled tomato and vegetable soup, has no ingredient list, and the lunch soups have been consommé or potage (2022 and 2023 reviews).
kyoto_chinon_nijojo_kojocho.hours_raw: Official site: dinner 17:30–22:00 (its information section gives 17:30–23:00, last order 22:00); lunch on Sundays 12:00–14:30 (last order 14:00; the top of the page says 12:00–14:00), and Monday–Saturday lunch for two or more by reservation made by the day before; closed irregularly. Tabelog gives 12:00–14:30 and 17:30–22:00 every day, with Mon–Sat lunch by reservation the day before. Children aged 10 and under are declined (official site; Tabelog: 5th grade and above). One drink per person (official menu). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 12 seats: counter and tables (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; BYO and takeout listed; no parking, coin parking nearby (Tabelog). On the north-east corner of Ogawa-dori and Oshikoji-dori, 8 min walk west of Karasuma-Oike Stn (official site). Opened 11 November 2019 (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_chinon_nijojo_kojocho.notes: [French bistro · Nijo Castle] A twelve-seat corner bistro east of Nijo Castle where the owner-chef, who trained in France from age 19, cooks and serves alone: terrines, Amakusa rock oysters, Kamo eggplant gratin and braised beef cheek à la carte, or an omakase course from ¥6,600. Dinner nightly; lunch on Sundays, other days by reservation.

chef_bio.background: The official profile: owner-chef 坂由紀夫 went alone to France at 19, trained in hotels and restaurants there and qualified as a cook, returned to Japan at 25, and worked in Kyoto, Tokyo and Osaka in French and also Italian restaurants and a steakhouse. Opened CHINON on 11 November 2019 (official site). The chef cooks and serves single-handed, so dishes can take time when busy (August 2024 review). Reviewers describe a chef of rugged looks with a warm smile (May 2023), kind and approachable (September 2024) and friendly (November 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: The official site: authentic French cooking by a France-trained chef with seasonal Kyoto ingredients, in a space of hospitality.
chef_bio.specialty: Country terrine; braised beef cheek; omakase course.

anecdotes.text: On a Sunday in January 2022 a diner came just after 13:30, the only customer, and had the ¥1,800 lunch with a house sausage and three kinds of house bread.
During Obon in August 2024 a couple walked in around 20:00 without a booking and, after a late lunch, chose the smallest omakase course, ¥6,600 with tax.
A family of nine celebrated a birthday here in September 2024, finishing with lamb chops and house desserts.
A diner who manages two or three visits a year wrote in November 2025 of a tempting à la carte menu and a friendly chef.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: フランス料理 シノン (CHINON)、中京区古城町369-3、小川通り押小路通り北東角、地下鉄烏丸御池駅より西へ徒歩8分。2019年11月11日オープン。オーナシェフ 坂由紀夫: 19歳で単身フランスへ、ホテル、レストランで修行、調理師免許取得、25歳で帰国、京都、東京、大阪でフランス料理のほかイタリア料理、ステーキハウスで経験を積む。ディナー17:30〜22:00 (ご案内の欄は17:30〜23:00、22:00ラストオーダー)、ランチは日曜12:00〜14:30、月〜土曜は前日までに2名以上で予約、不定休、10歳以下の子どもは遠慮。アラカルト (2024年8月2日更新、税込): ガスパッチョ880円、自家製田舎風テリーヌ2,090円、天草産岩牡蛎 生1,540円・焼き1,650円、鱧と万願寺唐辛子のアヒージョ2,200円、鴨茄子のグラタン1,980円、国産牛のほほ肉の煮込み4,290円、仔羊のロースト4,400円、お任せコース (2名から) 6,600円、ひとりワンドリンク。ランチ2,750円。食べログ: カード可、PayPay、12席、禁煙、車椅子可。口コミ (2020〜2025年、英語): シェフがひとりで料理とサービス (2024年8月)、テリーヌ、ほほ肉の煮込み、ラムチョップ、かためのプリン。

cultural_comfort.note: Menu dish names in French and Japanese (official site); the chef trained in France (official site). Phone service may be Japanese only (Tabelog).

kyoto_kappo_tb26039927_ebisugawa.gf_detail: Ask. Tempura, fried yam, grilled nama-fu, ponzu, Saikyo-miso grilled fish and red miso soup with wheat-gluten fu (2024–2026 reviews); no gluten or allergy information on Tabelog.
kyoto_kappo_tb26039927_ebisugawa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led kappo (Tabelog lists it as particular about fish) whose courses and lunch sets include sashimi, fugu and miso soups (2023–2026 reviews); no vegan option mentioned.
kyoto_kappo_tb26039927_ebisugawa.hours_raw: Tabelog: every day 11:00–14:00 (L.O. 13:30) and 17:00–22:00 (L.O. food 21:00, drinks 21:30); closed irregularly. Reservations taken (Tabelog). The menu with prices is shown outside (September and November 2024 reviews). Courses (Tabelog): ¥6,800 (7 dishes), ¥8,500 (8 dishes) and ¥13,500 (9 dishes, with Kuroge wagyu), plus hot-pot courses; à la carte also possible (December 2025 review). 16 seats: 6 at the counter, a table for two and two four-seat tables; partitioned rooms for 2–8, tatami and sunken seating (Tabelog); a tatami room at the back for 6–8 looking onto a small garden (October 2023, July 2025 and January 2026 reviews). Children welcome; wheelchair accessible; non-smoking; no parking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 265 m from Marutamachi subway Stn; about 5 min walk (Tabelog; July 2025 review). Opened 4 August 2023 (Tabelog).
kyoto_kappo_tb26039927_ebisugawa.notes: [Kappo · Ebisugawa] A sixteen-seat machiya kappo by Ebisugawa-dori, opened in 2023: lunch gozen of tempura or grilled fish with a lacquer box of obanzai for about ¥2,000, and dinner courses from ¥6,800 with fish, fugu and winter hot pots, or à la carte. A counter, tatami rooms and a small garden.

chef_bio.background: Opened 4 August 2023 (Tabelog). A May 2025 reviewer who had been head chef at a Kyoto restaurant more than ten years earlier wrote that the owner had cooked the simmered dishes there before opening this place. A December 2025 reviewer gave the owner's age as 45, quiet at work in a relaxed room; earlier reviewers found the chef cheerful (October 2023) and attentive, swapping a dessert on request (September 2024). An August 2023 reviewer appreciated the owner's stance of not leaning on gourmet sites, so that regulars do not find it hard to get in.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch gozen with hassun of obanzai; seasonal kappo courses; chicken hot pot in winter.

anecdotes.text: A diner who held a year-end party here in December 2024 took the staff's recommendation of the ¥7,000 chicken hot-pot course and found the generous portions a challenge for a fifty-something, finishing with a small serving of thin udon.
In May 2025 a former head chef dropped in for lunch alone; the owner, a former colleague not seen for about eight years, looked surprised and then broke into a big smile.
A March 2025 first-timer shared sake and takikomi gohan passed along by the regulars at the counter.
On a hot July 2025 day a diner squeezed in a ¥2,100 Saikyo-yaki gozen of flounder before going back to hospital for afternoon tests.
